(Section)

Among these is His, glory be to Him, swearing by ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it covers over﴾ in recognition of His bounty upon His Messenger, His honouring of him, and His giving him what pleases him. This entails His affirmation of him, so it is an oath affirming the soundness of his prophethood and affirming his recompense in the Hereafter; it is thus an oath concerning prophethood and the return (al-ma'ad). He swore by two great signs among His signs, which point to His lordship, His wisdom and His mercy: the night and the day.

Consider the correspondence between this oath and what is sworn to: the light of the forenoon (al-duha), which arrives after the darkness of the night, corresponds to what it swears to, namely the light of revelation, which came to him after its withholding from him, to the point that his enemies said, "Muhammad's Lord has forsaken him." So He swore by the brightness of the day after the darkness of the night, to the brightness and light of revelation after the darkness of its withholding and concealment. Moreover, He who splits the darkness of the night to reveal the light of the day is the One who split the darkness of ignorance and polytheism with the light of revelation and prophethood. These two are perceptible to the senses, and these two are perceptible to the intellect. Furthermore, He whose mercy required that He not leave His servants in the darkness of the night forever, but guided them by the light of day to their interests and livelihoods, is not fitting to leave them in the darkness of ignorance and error, but guides them by the light of revelation and prophethood to the interests of their worldly life and their Hereafter.

Consider the fine connection between what the oath is sworn by and what it is sworn to, and consider the eloquence and splendour upon these words, and the majesty upon their meanings.

He, glory be to Him, negated that He had bidden farewell to His Prophet or abandoned him (qala). "Tawdi'" means leaving, and "qalan" means hatred. He has not left him since He cared for him and honoured him, nor has He hated him since He loved him. And He, glory be to Him, stated absolutely that the Hereafter is better for him than the former life, and this encompasses every state to which He elevates him, each of which is better for him than what preceded it, just as the Abode of the Hereafter is better for him than what precedes it.

Then He promised him what would gladden his eye, delight his soul, and expand his breast: that He would give him, and he would be well pleased. This encompasses what He gives him of the Qur'an, guidance, victory, the abundance of those who follow him, the elevation of his mention and the exaltation of his word, what He gives him after his death, what He gives him on the standing of the Day of Resurrection, and what He gives him in Paradise. As for what the ignorant are deceived by, namely that he will not be pleased while a single member of his community is in the Fire, or that he will not be pleased for anyone of his community to enter the Fire, this is one of the deceptions of Satan towards them and a game he plays with them. Indeed, he (ﷺ) is pleased with what his Lord, blessed and exalted, is pleased with. Allah, glorified is He, causes to enter the Fire those who deserve it among the disbelievers and the disobedient, and then He sets for His Messenger a limit (for those he may) intercede for. His Messenger knows Him and His right better than to say, "I am not pleased that anyone of my community enter the Fire," as if He would leave them in it. Rather, his Lord, blessed and exalted, grants him permission, so he intercedes for whom Allah wills to be interceded for, and he does not intercede for anyone other than those for whom He has granted permission and whom He is pleased with.

**(Section: Being Deceived by a Corrupt Understanding)**

Among them are those who are deceived by a corrupt understanding that they, and others like them, have derived from the texts of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. They rely upon it, as some of them rely on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be well pleased﴾ [93:5].

He said: "He will not be pleased that anyone of his community be in the Fire." This is among the most ugly ignorance and the clearest lie against him, for he is pleased with what his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, is pleased with. Allah, the Exalted, pleases him by the punishment of the wrongdoers, the transgressors, the treacherous, and those who persist in the major sins. Far be it from His Messenger that he be pleased with what his Lord, blessed and exalted, is not pleased with.

And like some of them relying on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ [39:53].

This too is among the most ugly ignorance, for shirk (associating partners with Allah) is included in this verse, since it is the head and foundation of sins. There is no disagreement that this verse concerns those who repent: He forgives the sin of every repentant person, whatever sin it was. Had the verse concerned those who do not repent, all the texts of threat would be nullified.

And (they rely on) the hadiths about bringing out a people of the monotheists from the Fire through intercession (shafa'ah).

This person is only brought to this by the scarcity of his knowledge and understanding, for He, glorified is He, here generalized and left it unrestricted, so it is known that He intended the repentant. In Surat an-Nisa', He specified and restricted, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [4:48]. Thus Allah, glorified is He, informed that He does not forgive shirk, and informed that He forgives what is below it. Had this been concerning the repentant, He would not have distinguished between shirk and other than it.

And like the deception of some of the ignorant by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Most Generous?﴾ [82:6]. He says, "His generosity." Some of them even say: "He prompted the deceived with his argument." This is an ugly ignorance. What deceived him concerning his Lord was only deception (ghurur), namely Satan, his own commanding self that enjoins evil, his ignorance, and his desire. He, glorified is He, used the word "the Most Generous," and He is the Great, Mighty Lord who is obeyed, who should not be deceived by, nor should His right be neglected. So this deceived person placed deception in other than its proper place, and was deceived by one who should not be trusted.

And like the deception of some of them by the saying of the Exalted concerning the Fire: ﴿None will burn therein except the most wretched, who denied and turned away﴾ [92:15-16], and His saying: ﴿prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [2:24].

This deceived person did not realize that His saying ﴿I have warned you of a Fire blazing﴾ [92:14] refers to a specific Fire among the levels of Hell. Even if it were all of Hell, He, glorified is He, did not say "he will not enter it," but said ﴿None will burn therein except the most wretched﴾. Not burning in it does not necessarily entail not entering it, for burning (salyy) is more specific than entering, and negating the more specific does not entail negating the more general.

Furthermore, had this deceived person reflected upon the verse that follows it, he would have known that he is not included in it, so it is not guaranteed for him that he will be spared from it.

As for His saying concerning the Fire, ﴿prepared for the disbelievers﴾, He said concerning Paradise: ﴿prepared for the righteous﴾ [3:133]. The preparation of the Fire for the disbelievers does not preclude the entry of the sinners and wrongdoers into it, and the preparation of Paradise for the righteous does not preclude the entry of one who has in his heart even an atom's weight of faith and has never done a good deed.

And like the deception of some of them regarding fasting the Day of 'Ashura' or the Day of 'Arafah, to the extent that some say: "The Day of 'Ashura' expiates all the sins of the year, and fasting the Day of 'Arafah remains an increase in reward." This deceived person did not realize that fasting Ramadan and the five prayers are greater and more sublime than fasting the Day of 'Arafah and the Day of 'Ashura', and they only expiate what is between them when the major sins are avoided.

Ramadan to Ramadan, and Friday to Friday, are not capable of expiating minor sins unless the abandonment of major sins is combined with them. Then the combination of the two matters becomes capable of expiating minor sins.

How, then, could the fasting of a voluntary day expiate every major sin the servant has committed while he persists in it and has not repented of it? This is impossible. Yet it is not impossible that the fasting of the Day of 'Arafah and the Day of 'Ashura expiates all the sins of the year in its generality, and that it is among the texts of promise that have conditions and impediments, and that his persistence in major sins is an impediment to expiation. So when he does not persist in major sins, the fasting and the non-persistence assist each other and cooperate in general expiation, just as Ramadan and the five prayers, together with avoiding major sins, assist each other and cooperate in expiating minor sins. Moreover, He, glorified is He, has said: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾ [4:31].

It is thus known that making a thing a cause of expiation does not prevent it from assisting another cause in expiation, and that expiation, when two causes combine, is stronger and more complete than when one of them stands alone. Whenever the causes of expiation grow stronger, it becomes stronger, more complete, and more comprehensive.

And like some of them relying on his saying ﷺ, relating from his Lord: "I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think of Me what he wills," meaning: whatever he assumes of Me, I will do with him accordingly. There is no doubt that good opinion of Allah occurs only together with good deeds, for the one who does good is one who thinks well of his Lord: that He will reward him for his goodness, not break His promise, and accept his repentance.

As for the evildoer who persists in major sins, wrongdoing, and transgressions, the loneliness of sins, wrongdoing, and what is forbidden prevents him from having good opinion of his Lord. This exists in observable reality: the runaway slave who has departed from his master's obedience does not think well of him, and the desolation of wrongdoing never coexists with good opinion. The evildoer feels estranged in proportion to his evil, and the best of people in their opinion of their Lord are the most obedient to Him.

As al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The believer thinks well of his Lord, so he does good deeds; and the wicked person thinks ill of his Lord, so he does evil deeds."

How could one who turns away from Him, who dwells and roams in what angers Him and displeases Him, who exposes himself to His curse, whose right and command have become so insignificant to him that he neglects them, and whose prohibition has become so trivial to him that he commits it and persists in it, have good opinion of his Lord? How could one who wages war against Him, opposes His friends, allies with His enemies, denies the attributes of His perfection, thinks ill of what He has described Himself with and what His Messenger ﷺ has described Him with, and in his ignorance supposes that the apparent meaning of that is misguidance and disbelief, have good opinion of his Lord? How could one who thinks that He does not speak, does not command, does not forbid, is not pleased, and does not become angry have good opinion of his Lord?

Concerning one who doubted that His hearing encompasses some particulars, even secret speech, Allah has said: ﴿And that is your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers﴾ [41:23].

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 93, verses 6–8:**

Then Allah, glorified is He, mentioned His blessings upon him: sheltering him after he was an orphan, guiding him after he was astray, and enriching him after he was poor. He had been in need of someone to shelter, guide, and enrich him, so his Lord sheltered him, guided him, and enriched him. Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to repay these three blessings with the thanks that befits them. He forbade him to oppress the orphan, to rebuff the beggar, and to conceal the blessing, but rather to speak of it. He also enjoined him to care for orphans, the poor, and seekers of knowledge. Mujahid and Muqatil said: "Do not belittle the orphan, for you were an orphan yourself." Al-Farra' said: "Do not oppress him regarding his wealth, so that you take his right because of his weakness." This is what the Arabs used to do regarding orphans: they would take their wealth and wrong them. So the address was made harsh concerning the orphan, and likewise whoever has no helper is to be treated harshly in this matter. This is a prohibition addressed to all who are legally responsible.

﴿And as for the beggar, do not rebuff him﴾.

Most exegetes said: this refers to the one who asks for kindness and charity. Do not rebuff him when he asks you, for you were once poor. Then either give to him, or turn him away gently. Al-Hasan said: "Indeed, he is not the beggar who comes to you, but the seeker of knowledge." This is also the view of Yahya ibn Adam, who said: "When the seeker of knowledge comes to you, do not rebuff him."

The correct position is that the verse encompasses both types.

**(Benefit)**

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? And find you lost and guide you?﴾

The interpretation of this verse is by the verse at the end of Surah al-Shura. If the most intellectual of Allah's creation, absolutely, attained guidance only through revelation, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: If I am astray, I am astray only against myself; and if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me﴾ [Saba': 50].

So how could the foolish of intellect, the dull of wit, and the scatterbrained attain the realities of faith merely by their own minds, without the texts of the prophets? ﴿You have certainly produced a horrendous thing. The heavens are about to rupture from it, the earth to split apart, and the mountains to collapse in ruin﴾.

**(Section)**

Ali ibn Abi Rabah al-Lakhmi said: "I was with Maslamah ibn Mukhallad al-Ansari, who was then governor of Egypt, and Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'As was sitting with him. Maslamah quoted a line of poetry by Abu Talib and said: 'If Abu Talib had seen what we are in today of Allah's blessing and honour, he would have known that his nephew, the master, had come with good.' Abdullah ibn Amr said, and at that time he was a noble master who had come with good. Maslamah said: 'Did not Allah, the Exalted, say: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? And find you lost and guide you? And find you in need and enrich you?﴾'"

Abdullah ibn Amr said: "As for the orphan, he was an orphan of both his parents. As for destitution ('ayla), all that was in the hands of the Arabs was little. He said that the Arabs were all in need until Allah opened it to him and to the Arabs who embraced Islam and entered the religion of Allah in throngs. Then Allah took him before he took anything of it, and he passed on and left it, warning against it and its trials." He said: "This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied﴾."

The world would never have pleased him, and he did not desire it all for his community. He warned against it, and it was offered to him, but he refused it. Rather, what he was given was the reward, and what was opened for him and his community, such as the kingdoms of Chosroes and Caesar, and people entering Islam, and the religion becoming manifest. If that was his love and his pleasure, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from al-Awza'i, from Isma'il ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said:

"I saw what would be opened after me, city by city, and it pleased me. So there was revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied﴾."

He said: "I will be given a thousand palaces of pearls, whose soil is musk, and in each palace is what is fitting for him."

They said: As for what you mentioned about renunciation of the world and frugality in it, renunciation does not contradict wealth. Indeed, the renunciation of the wealthy is more complete than the renunciation of the poor, for the wealthy renounces from power, while the poor renounces from weakness, and between them is a great distance. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was, in his state of wealth, the most renunciant of creation. Likewise, Abraham the Friend had much wealth, yet he was the most renunciant of people in the world.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated in his Jami' from the hadith of Abu Dharr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said:

"Renunciation of the world is not prohibiting what is lawful, nor squandering it. Rather, renunciation of the world is that what is in your hands is not more trusted by you than what is in the hand of Allah, and that you are more eager for the reward of a calamity when you are afflicted by it than you would be if it had remained for you."

Imam Ahmad was asked about a man who has a thousand dinars, and whether he can be a renunciant. He said: "Yes, on condition that he does not rejoice when they increase, nor grieve when they decrease."

Some of the early Muslims said: "The renunciant is one whose gratitude is not overwhelmed by lawful things, nor his patience by unlawful things."

This is one of the finest definitions: a reality composed of patience and gratitude. Whoever does not possess both does not deserve the name of renunciant.

So whoever's gratitude prevails over what is made abundant for him of lawful things, and whose patience prevails over what befalls him of unlawful things, he is the renunciant in truth. This is unlike one whose gratitude is overwhelmed by lawful things and whose patience is overwhelmed by unlawful things, so his gratitude and patience are both defeated. Such a person is not a renunciant.

**(Section)**

Abu Hafs was asked: "With what does the poor man come before his Lord?" He said: "The poor man has nothing to come before his Lord with except his poverty."

The reality of poverty and its perfection, as some of them said when he was asked: "When does the poor man deserve the name of poverty?" He said: "When no remnant of himself remains in him." It was said to him: "How is that?" He said: "If he has something, then he does not have it. If he does not have it, then it is his."

This is one of the finest expressions of the meaning of poverty to which the people (the Sufis) refer: that all of him belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and no remnant of himself, his portion, or his desire remains in him. Whenever something of the rulings of his own self remains in him, his poverty is flawed.

Then it was explained by his saying: "If he has something, then he does not have it," meaning: if it belongs to his self, then it does not belong to Allah. And if it does not belong to his self, then it belongs to Allah.

So the reality of poverty is that you do not belong to yourself, and nothing of yourself belongs to it, such that you are wholly for Allah.

And if you belong to yourself, then there is possession and self-sufficiency, which contradicts poverty.

This poverty to which they refer is not contradicted by wealth or possessions. The messengers of Allah and His prophets were at its peak despite their wealth and their possessions, such as Abraham the Friend (ﷺ), who was the father of guests, and who had wealth and livestock. Likewise were Solomon and David, peace be upon them. Likewise was our Prophet (ﷺ), as Allah said: ﴿And He found you in need and enriched you﴾ [al-Duha: 8].

They were rich in their poverty and poor in their richness.

True poverty is the continuance of need for Allah in every state, and that the servant witnesses, in every particle of his outward and inward being, complete need for Allah, the Exalted, in every respect.

Poverty is essential to the servant, and it is only renewed for him as a state through his witnessing and his existence; otherwise it is a reality.

As Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah sanctify his spirit, said:

*"Poverty is for me an attribute of essence, perpetually binding,*
*just as wealth is forever an essential attribute of Him."*

**[Section: The Station of Richness]**

Among the stations of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ is the station of lofty richness.

It has two kinds: richness through Allah, and richness free from other than Allah. These two are the reality of poverty. But the people of the path (Sufis) made richness a station of its own.

The author of *Al-Manazil* (Al-Harawi), may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The chapter on richness. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And He found you in need and enriched you﴾ [al-Duha: 8]."

In the verse there are three opinions:

The first: that He enriched him with wealth after his poverty. This is the view of most exegetes, because He paired it with His saying "in need" (ā'il), and the one in need is the one who lacks, not the one with destitution. So He enriched him with wealth.

The second: that He pleased him with what He gave him, and made him rich with it over other than it. This is richness of heart and soul, not richness of wealth, and it is the reality of richness.

The third, which is the correct one: that it encompasses both kinds of richness. He enriched his heart with it, and He enriched him with wealth.

Then he said: "Richness is a name for complete possession."

That is, whoever possesses in one respect but not in another is not rich. On this basis, the name "the Rich" truly belongs only to Allah. Everything other than Him is poor in need of Him by its very essence.

**[Degrees of Richness]**

**[The First Degree: Richness of the Heart]**

He said: "It has three degrees. The first degree: richness of the heart. It is its safety from the cause, its peace with the decree, and its freedom from dispute."

The reality of richness of the heart is its attachment to Allah alone. The reality of its blameworthy poverty is its attachment to other than Him.

When it is attached to Allah, these three things that he mentioned are attained for it.

"Its safety from the cause" means from attachment to it, not from carrying it out. For the people of heedlessness, richness is in the cause, and for this reason their hearts are attached to it. For the knowers, it is in the Causer. Likewise with craft and strength.

These three are the aspects of richness in the eyes of people. They are what the Prophet (ﷺ) pointed to in his saying:

"Charity is not lawful for a rich person, nor for one with sound strength."

In another narration: "nor for a strong earner." Richness in a thing: its possessor is rich by it when his soul is at rest with it. But if his rest is in his Lord, then he is rich through Him. Whatever the soul rests in, it is poor in need of it.

As for peace with the decree, it is of two kinds:

The first: peace with the religious, commanded ruling, which is embracing it and agreeing with it, as opposed to fighting against it.

The second: peace with the universal, predestined ruling, which befalls him without his choice, and he has no power to repel it, and he is not commanded to repel it.

In peace with the ruling there is a point that is essential: stripping its attribution and ascription from the one from whom it proceeds, such that he does not attribute it to anyone else.

This includes the Tawhid of Lordship in peace with the universal ruling, and the Tawhid of Divinity in peace with the religious ruling. These two are the reality of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾.

As for freedom from dispute, it is only praised when it is freedom from dispute by oneself for oneself. But if one disputes through Allah and for Allah, this is from the perfection of servitude. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say in his opening supplication:

"O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, upon You I have relied, to You I have turned in repentance, through You I have disputed, and to You I have referred judgment."

**[The Second Degree: Richness of the Soul]**

He said: "The second degree: richness of the soul. It is its being firm upon what is desired, its safety from personal desires, and its freedom from showing off."

The Shaykh made the richness of the soul above the richness of the heart.

It is known that matters of the heart are more complete and stronger than matters of the soul. But in this order there is a subtle point: the soul is among the soldiers and subjects of the heart. It is among the most fierce of its soldiers in opposing it and dissenting from it. Through it the kingdom is disturbed, and the intruder enters upon it. When perfection is attained for the heart through richness, it is not complete except through the richness of the soul as well. For whenever the soul is poor, the judgment of its poverty returns upon the heart, and its richness is disturbed. So the richness of the soul is a completion of the richness of the heart and its perfection. And the richness of the heart is essentially through the richness of the soul. The second: peace with the universal, predestined ruling, which befalls him without his choice, and he has no power to repel it, and he is not commanded to repel it.

In peace with the ruling there is a point that is essential: stripping its attribution and ascription from the one from whom it proceeds, such that he does not attribute it to anyone else.

This includes the Tawhid of Lordship in peace with the universal ruling, and the Tawhid of Divinity in peace with the religious ruling. These two are the reality of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾.

As for freedom from dispute, it is only praised when it is freedom from dispute by oneself for oneself. But if one disputes through Allah and for Allah, this is from the perfection of servitude. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say in his opening supplication:

"O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, upon You I have relied, to You I have turned in repentance, through You I have disputed, and to You I have referred judgment."

**[The Second Degree: Richness of the Soul]**

He said: "The second degree: richness of the soul. It is its being firm upon what is desired, its safety from personal desires, and its freedom from showing off."

The Shaykh made the richness of the soul above the richness of the heart.

It is known that matters of the heart are more complete and stronger than matters of the soul. But in this order there is a subtle point: the soul is among the soldiers and subjects of the heart. It is among the most fierce of its soldiers in opposing it and dissenting from it. Through it the kingdom is disturbed, and the intruder enters upon it. When perfection is attained for the heart through richness, it is not complete except through the richness of the soul as well. For whenever the soul is poor, the judgment of its poverty returns upon the heart, and its richness is disturbed. So the richness of the soul is a completion of the richness of the heart and its perfection. And the richness of the heart is essentially through the richness of the soul. Richness reaches the soul from the heart, and poverty, harm and distress reach the heart from the soul.

Having known this, the Shaykh made the richness of the soul consist of three things:

Its being firm upon what is desired, which is the Truth, the Exalted. Its firmness upon Him is the continuance of seeking Him and cutting off the stages through journeying toward Him.

Second: its safety from personal desires, which are its outward and inward attachments to other than Allah.

Third: its freedom from showing off, which is intending other than Allah by any of its deeds or words. Its showing off is evidence of the severity of its poverty, and its attachment to desires is also from its poverty.

And its failure to be firm upon the true object of its seeking is also from its poverty, and that indicates that it has not found Allah. For if it had found Him, it would have been firm in journeying toward Him, cut off its attachments and desires from other than Him, and would not have intended other than Him by its deeds.

These three things are only firm for one who has attained his self and found his object. As long as he has not found his Lord, the Exalted, there is no firmness for him, no safety for his soul from desires, and no freedom for it from showing off.

**[Section: The Third Degree: Richness Through the Truth]**

He said: "The third degree: richness through the Truth. It has three stages. The first stage: witnessing His remembrance of you. The second: continuance in contemplating His primacy. The third: attaining His existence."

As for witnessing His remembrance of you, it has been mentioned shortly before.

As for contemplating His primacy, it is His preceding all things. He is the First, before whom there is nothing.

Some of them said: "I have not seen anything except that I have seen Allah before it."

If you say: What richness comes to the heart from contemplating the primacy of the Lord and His precedence over everything? It is known that this is attained by everyone, rich or poor. So what is the aspect of the richness attained by it?

I say: When the heart witnesses His precedence over causes, and that they were in the realm of non-existence, and He is the One who clothed them in the garment of existence, then they are non-existent in essence, poor in need of Him in essence. And He is the Existent by His essence, rich by His essence, not by other than Himself. So richness in reality is only through Him, just as it is in reality only for Him. Richness through other than Him is the very essence of poverty, for it is richness through a non-existent poor thing. How can a poor thing become rich through another poor thing like itself?

As for attaining His existence, it is the indication of all the people (Sufis) to this meaning. It is the end of their journey. In the divine narration: "Son of Adam, seek Me and you will find Me. If you find Me, you will find everything. If you miss Me, you will miss everything. And I am more beloved to you than everything."

And whoever does not know the meaning of His existence for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and attaining Him, let him throw ashes on his head, weep over himself. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 93, verse 11:

Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet to speak of his Lord's blessing, saying: ﴿But as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it.﴾

Allah the Exalted loves that His servant should show the trace of His blessing upon him, for that is thanking Him by the tongue of one's state.

Ali ibn al-Ja'd said: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri say: Dawud, peace be upon him, said, "Praise be to Allah with praise befitting the nobility of His Face and the majesty of His Glory." So Allah revealed to him, "O Dawud, you have wearied the angels."

Shu'bah said: Al-Mufaddal ibn Fadalah narrated to us from Abu Raja' al-Utaridi, who said: "Imran ibn Husain came out to us wearing a silk cloak (mutarraf khazz) which we had never seen on him before or after, and he said: The Messenger of Allah said:

"When Allah bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see the trace of His blessing upon His servant."

In the written collection of Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet, he said:

"Eat, drink, and give in charity without arrogance or extravagance, for Allah loves to see the trace of His blessing upon His servant."

Shu'bah also mentioned, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from his father, who said:

"I came to the Messenger of Allah while I was in shabby appearance. He said, 'Do you have any wealth?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'From what kind of wealth?' I said, 'From all kinds: Allah has given me camels, horses, slaves, and sheep.' He said, 'When Allah gives you wealth, let it be seen upon you.'"

In some mursal reports: "Allah loves to see the trace of His blessing upon His servant in his food and his drink."

Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated from Abu Ma'mar, from Bukayr ibn Abd Allah, raising it (to the Prophet):

"Whoever is given good and it is seen upon him is named 'the beloved of Allah,' one who speaks of Allah's blessing; and whoever is given good and it is not seen upon him is named 'the hated of Allah,' one who opposes Allah's blessing."

Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: "It used to be said: Whoever recognizes Allah's blessing in his heart and praises Him with his tongue has not completed that until he sees the increase, due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.﴾"

And he said: "From the thanks for a blessing is that one speaks of it."

Allah the Exalted has said:

"O son of Adam, when you are rolling in My blessings while you are rolling in disobedience to Me, then beware of Me, lest I throw you down among your sins. O son of Adam, fear Me and sleep wherever you wish."

Al-Sha'bi said: Gratitude is half of faith, and certainty is the whole of faith.

Abu Qilabah said: "Let not a worldly life that you have thanked God for harm you."

Al-Hasan said: When Allah bestows blessings upon a people, He asks them for gratitude; when they are grateful, He is able to increase them. And when they are ungrateful, He is able to turn His blessing against them as punishment. Allah has censured the kanud, who is one who does not thank for His blessings.

Al-Hasan said regarding ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord﴾: he counts the calamities and forgets the blessings.

The Prophet ﷺ informed that women are the majority of the people of the Fire for this reason. He said:

"If you were to be good to one of them all your life, then she saw something from you, she would say, 'I have never seen any good from you at all.'" So if this is the case for abandoning thanks for the blessing of a husband, when in reality it is from Allah, then what of one who abandons thanks for the blessing of Allah?

O you who are unjust in his deed, and injustice is returned upon the one who wronged,

How long will you, and until when, complain of calamities and forget the blessings?

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned, from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah said:

"Speaking of blessing is thanks, and abandoning it is disbelief. Whoever does not thank for little does not thank for much. Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah. Congregation is blessing and division is punishment."

(Section)

Regarding this command to speak of blessing, there are two views.

The first: that it refers to mentioning the blessing and reporting it, such as saying: "Allah has bestowed upon me such and such." Muqatil said: It means give thanks for the blessings mentioned to you in this surah: the mending of orphanhood, guidance after misguidance, and enrichment after poverty.

Speaking of Allah's blessing is thanks, as in the marfu' hadith of Jabir:

"Whoever is shown a kindness should repay it. If he finds nothing to repay it with, then let him praise (the giver). For when he praises him, he has thanked him. And whoever conceals it has been ungrateful. And whoever adorns himself with what he has not been given is like one wearing two garments of falsehood."

Here he mentioned the three categories of people: the thankful one who praises the blessing, the one who denies it, and the one who conceals it. And the one who displays that he is among its possessors when he is not among them: he is adorned with what he has not been given.

And in another marfu' report:

"Whoever does not thank for little does not thank for much. Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah. Speaking of Allah's blessing is thanks, and abandoning it is disbelief. The congregation is mercy and division is punishment."

The second view: that the speaking of blessing commanded in this verse is calling to Allah, conveying His message, and teaching the community.

Mujahid said: it is prophethood. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, convey what you were sent with, and speak of the prophethood which Allah has given you.

Al-Kalbi said: it is the Qur'an. He commanded him to recite it.

The correct view is that it encompasses both types, since each of them is a blessing commanded to be thanked for, spoken of, and made manifest, and making it manifest is part of thanking for it.

He said in al-Tibyan:

"And His saying ﴿But as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it.﴾

Mujahid said: with the Qur'an.

Al-Kalbi said: meaning make it manifest; the Qur'an is the greatest blessing Allah has bestowed upon him, so He commanded him to recite it and teach it.

Abu Bishr narrated from Mujahid: Speak of the prophethood which Allah has given you.

Al-Zajjaj said: Convey what you were sent with, and speak of the prophethood which He has given you, and it is the most glorious of blessings.

Muqatil said: Give thanks for this blessing mentioned in this surah.

The verification is that blessings encompass all of this, so He commanded him not to rebuff one who asks for kindness and knowledge, and to speak of Allah's blessings upon him in religion and in worldly life."

[Section: The difference between speaking of Allah's blessings and boasting of them]

The difference between speaking of Allah's blessings and boasting of them: the one who speaks of a blessing reports the attributes of its Bestower and His pure generosity and kindness, so he praises Him by making it manifest. Speaking of it, thankful to Him and spreading all that He has granted, is intended to make manifest Allah's attributes, His praise and glorification, and to move the soul to seek from Him alone, to love Him and hope in Him. Thus he is one who turns to Allah by manifesting and spreading His blessings and speaking of them.

As for boasting of blessings: it is that one exalts himself over people with them, showing them that he is mightier and greater than they, so he mounts their necks, captures their hearts, and draws them to himself through veneration and service.

Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir said: Indeed, Satan has snares and traps, and among his snares and traps are arrogance over Allah's blessings, pride over the servants of Allah, boasting of Allah's gift, and humiliation in what is not for the sake of Allah.
